items.title: A Review of SHRINCs - Project Eleven
items.text:
Project Eleven published a review of the SHRINCs proposal today. SHRINCs is a hash-based, stateful scheme for post-quantum signatures https://stacker.news/items/1555802/r/Scoresby, https://stacker.news/items/1546995/r/Scoresby, that relies on SHA256 and one-time use signatures.

Project Eleven's review points out a number of the benefits of the [SHRINCs proposal](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/blob/main/SHRINCS.md):

> - SHRINCS is instantiated entirely with SHA-256, so it introduces no new family of mathematical assumptions into Bitcoin.
> - the best-known quantum attack on a hash function, Grover's algorithm, gives a far smaller speedup than Shor's algorithm gives against ECDSA
> - SHA-256 is heavily optimized, hardware acceleration is widely available, and the verification cost per byte is low.

But, they ultimately come to the conclusion that SHRINC isn't quite right:

> Even though SHRINCS is meant to be a solution to the problem of securing Bitcoin in the post-quantum era, a primary design goal of SHRINCS seems to be optimizing block space, a shared and currently abundant resource. In doing so, it introduces a potential failure mode that is silent, irreversible, and borne by individuals at the exact layer where their money lives.

They claim that the statefulness requirement of SHRINCs (you really, really don't want to use the same signature twice) puts a lot of burden on wallets to get the implementation correct:

> The signer has to maintain a counter that only ever moves forward, to ensure that no signature is ever used twice. If the same state is used to sign two different messages, the same one-time key is reused, potentially breaking the security of the scheme and allowing an attacker to forge signatures and steal funds. 

In the nightmare scenario, you restore your wallet from a backup and the backup doesn't include the fully up to date state with the result that you leak your private key when you spend because you accidentally reused a signature.

SHRINCs does have a stateless signing mode that can be used if you are worried that you are inaccurate in your state of the wallet, but it creates a much larger signature.

Project Eleven's review points out three cases where statefulness becomes a footgun:

> Consider a hardware wallet. An attacker gets a copy of the device's encrypted SHRINCS state. The owner then signs a transaction, moving the counter forward. If the attacker can later restore the old state to the device, the wallet can reuse a WOTS+C leaf the next time it signs. The attacker does not need to extract the private key. All they need is the ability to roll back security-critical state.
> 
> Software wallets have a more mundane version of the same problem: backups. Let's consider a scenario where a wallet is backed up to iCloud. The user signs transactions and advances the SHRINCS state, later loses their phone, and restores an older backup. Unless the wallet has some independent rollback-resistant mechanism, its local state is now behind the actual signing history. No attacker required. Normal disaster recovery creates exactly the condition SHRINCS is trying to prevent.
> 
> Seed portability raises a similar issue. Bitcoin users expect to be able to restore a seed into another wallet. A seed can recover the SHRINCS secret material, but it cannot tell the new wallet which stateful WOTS+C leaves have already been used. The BIP handles this correctly by requiring stateless signing when the counter is unavailable or uncertain.

Ultimately, the Project Eleven people conclude:

> In our view, SHRINCS is elegant engineering, and evidence that serious people in the Bitcoin community are taking Q-Day seriously. But the case for the additional benefits, and complexity, that statefulness brings is not primarily a security argument. It is largely an attempt to avoid a political one.

And that a blocksize increase should be on the table (because many quantum resistant signatures are much larger, proposals like SHRINCs have optimized for size and, Project Eleven claims, introduced trade-offs).

One of the SHRINCs authors, n1ckler, has [already responded](https://x.com/n1ckler/status/2102850980744462625). While he agrees with a number of the things the Project Eleven guys are saying, n1ckler notes:

> The review suggests that the stateful path lets the SHRINCS authors say the block-size concern has been addressed. The intent is rather that SHRINCS doesn't depend on a block-size increase, so that question can be discussed separately without holding up post-quantum signatures. 
>
> The review describes stateful signing as an optimization, which fits better than the BIP's "primary path" wording. It also made me realize that calling the stateless path a "fallback" is misleading, and we're considering changing the terminology in the BIP.

It's an interesting conversation and worth spending half an hour reading through if you want to stay up on the latest quantum readiness stuff.

items.title: Local Bitcoiners - Cooking up community at Nostr Valley w/Seth
items.text: Seth joins Rev and Reed to talk about Nostr Valley, the annual Central Pennsylvania gathering he and Derek Ross have grown from a patched-together first year at Happy Valley Brewing into a free three-day event returning October 17th, plus Zap Cooking, the Nostr recipe platform he built around food as the base layer of culture. The conversation works through why hodl culture sent the wrong message, why a Nostr meetup is a Bitcoin meetup, and how remixing open source code is the same move as remixing your grandmother's pickle recipe. Rev ties it back to the nine forms of capital: when you spend financial capital to get people in a room, what comes back is trust, friendship, and collaboration you could never have bought.

items.title: [Did You Know] There's always a point on the earth where...
items.text:
... where the temperature and pressure are exactly the same as on the opposite side of the earth?

This happens at every point in time, throughout the history of the earth.

And what's weird is, if stand on that point and heat it up, then this magic point simply moves to another location.  There becomes a different location where the temperature and pressure are exactly the same on opposite sides of the earth.

This weird fact is a consequence of the **Borsuk-Ulam Theorem** which says that any continous function from a sphere to a plane must send some pair of opposite points to the same value.

Intuitively, it's actually pretty easy to explain in lower dimensions.

Imagine you're standing at the equator of the earth and measuring the temperature difference between the point you're standing and the point on the opposite side.  Let's say you currently measure +5°C difference.  That means when you stand on the opposite side, the difference would be -5°C.

Well, now start walking along the equator to the opposite side.  Since you're walking from a temperature differential of +5°C to -5°C, and since temperature varies continuously, at some point you'll pass a point where the temperature differential is 0°C, which means the two sides of the earth have exactly the same temperature.

It works with any continuous measure too.  So not only is there a point where temperature and pressure are the same on the two opposite sides, there's also a point where the temperature and humidity are the same, or a point where pressure and humidity are the same.  Or any measurement which is continuous in space that you can think of, even something like the average distance to the nearest human.

items.title: How would you acquire a new language?
items.text:
I want to learn Dutch.

Since it’s similar to German, I understand it when I read it (or I press random buttons at the self-checkout until I do), but when I hear it, I’m from a different planet, and not from the neighbouring country. If someone is talking to me, then I smile awkwardly and ask in English if they could repeat it in German or English. I still don’t know if it would actually make more sense to ask this in German because of the similarities, but since I struggle with understanding Dutch as a German, it’s probably the other way around, too. I’m also used to defaulting to English the moment I cross the German border. Anyway.

Since the [2140](https://2140.dev/) office is in Amsterdam, with many regular and visiting cool people, I consider learning Dutch a great investment. I’ve been in the Netherlands for more than two months now, and I’m finally embarrassed enough. My current Airbnb host struggles with English, so we tried to talk to each other with Google Translate. I wanted to tell her that she could also speak into the translator, but the whole situation was already messy enough, so I just patiently waited until she finished her message in Dutch and fixed all her typos. When I could read in English what she wanted to tell me (it was what I already thought but wasn’t sure), we were both so relieved that we gave each other a high five and laughed. The situation was so ridiculous that we almost started to just use hand movements. One time I didn’t even know the name for dustpan in German or English, so I just made the hand movement on the ground and she *immediately* understood it. That was fun, but I made a mental note to seriously learn Dutch and not just wing it and continue putting other people in this situation. Anyway, again.

In January, I used Duolingo to learn a bit of Portuguese for bitcoin++ in Brazil. It helped, but I was still completely stranded. My Portuguese and the *airport* staff’s English were almost not good enough to order a hamburger. Duolingo prepared me to become a barista with sentences like “Um café ou um chá?”

A few weeks ago, I read [this](https://niftys.substack.com/p/nifty-no-japan) from @niftynei in 2024:

> @jack posted a [really amazing YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=illApgaLgGA) that really nicely encapsulates how I think about learning languages: acquiring them, not learning them. I’ve been complaining for a while about how ineffective I find most apps for languages. I really want to try this story-telling exercise they suggest in the video, with German.

I asked her if she got the chance to try this out. She said she found [this website](https://www.thegermanproject.com/stories) where someone does exactly this! So now I wonder: is there a similar website for Dutch?? I haven’t found one yet, so I started to use Duolingo again.

Anyway, anyway, anyway. A lot of words to ask you: how would you ~learn~ acquire a new language?

Mark Carney - A master of statecraft in an era short of great orators
items.text:
![](https://m.stacker.news/158532)

**OPINION:** For the past decade, global diplomacy has been dictated by one man’s social media musings. Since Donald Trump first glided into the Trump Tower atrium on his golden escalator, he – and what he has to say – has been the story, **throwing red meat to the media and shaping the affairs of the US and the wider world through reactions to his increasingly imperial pronouncements.**

But the 47th US president has been off-key of late, and his outbursts on everything from tariffs to the war in Iran have sent his [popularity tumbling](https://yougov.com/en-gb/articles/55574-how-popular-is-donald-trump-in-europe-august-2026), not least in Europe where just 8% of Italians have a positive view of him, 10% of Germans and 13% of us in the UK.

**As Trump fever has cooled, one man has stepped forward to fill the ethical void. The Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, has taken a stand against his bothersome southern neighbour and, in so doing, has reoriented the free world’s moral compass.**

**Instead of looking to Washington DC for global leadership, global democracies are increasingly looking to the middle power man in Ottawa.**

Carney is a [banker](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/about) – or at least that was the world’s view of him until recently. He was governor of the Bank of Canada during the financial crisis of 2008, before leading the Bank of England from 2013-2020.

He only became a politician when elected leader of the Canadian Liberal Party in March 2025 and ensuring his mandate through a [landslide national election win](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2025/04/29/vote-count-begins-in-canada-snap-election-defined-by-trump-s-trade-war-and-threats_6740717_4.html?srsltid=AU7gw4XV88AbV2mmTrlg_6rN_pjpVWGet_O0Cmr_CoYnjo3NfhpcCZeS) the following month. But he has quickly emerged as a voice of political reason against the continued waves of Trump tirades.

Last week Carney [addressed the European parliament](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/speeches/2026/09/17/prime-minister-carney-delivers-address-european-parliament) following EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen’s support for a proposal for Canada to become the [EU’s first “associate member”](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjwyzrr9d3dko). Much like his speech in [Davos](https://theconversation.com/one-venue-two-speeches-how-mark-carney-left-donald-trump-in-the-dust-in-davos-274062) in January, Carney noted the current “geopolitical rupture”.

And, much like that Davos speech, he was calm, eloquent and displayed rare intellectual insight over how that rupture might be overcome. At Davos, he emphasised the need for middle powers to step up to the plate. Last week in Strasbourg, he added flesh to the bones, stressing how Canada and the EU had complementary strengths. He made the case for a deeper partnership based on cooperation, delivering seamless digital trade in many goods and services, underpinned by people-to-people ties including the free movement of young people.

The Canadian PM laid out a vision where Canada and the EU were allied by “common values, our compatible systems and complementary strengths”. While it’s early days in the discussion of a Canada-EU relationship, it was a seductive pitch to “create a beacon for other democracies”.

![Mark Carney and President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola in a joint news conference at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, last week.](https://www.thepress.co.nz/media/images/9Tzi8ywRz924XE3uHaD6DZ3Ef+IdbOiYlvIROR5vlqUSeZYZbm+SU0zjMnNqDfql8Yk4r+Ht43oxrl86VwI5IF7k1TZFVP%2FGWCLS2aI+JHF3cII+84huowmPhFf2sylmzs556jWYSX3nqKjqwMSQfxXR10gZwKCCCX3n5oPURxhg+ClYcD6QZEYKzs50Qch9La9XgAELt9YWggslkEb2pyUV3wLlZPJdZF5P+t+Ym64Ks9CYNicf562tRrUAiBA%2FdnLrca3C1UTDJPP8m9SnIh3subirJRxr1FqwDyFbDgTNEMwtmcp2CzwtorLWQgHWCi6hhTI0DT1%2F37NXETfdaRAVwOjPDK+JBIaRyL%2FWxaeVYCEQ5oJVBZfOlpy6j0JCtO5lVwqj9GymU+m+VuYnIBoukZkieXC8rvfLTbGLmBAvJvPKLXigzgcU+%2FJxQNAV%2Fj7+rSvt3J%2FHCcKSNog3%2FrkX%2FuGxSa6PIUusjX6IkS03VkbE9Ut+jFCZA%2FFEzh8DXLaMegfoSdQPTufodyuEGg==)

Trump was not mentioned by name in the speech but was clearly listening and clearly [riled](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yIeUaoHwUDk). Amid a trade war with its northern neighbour, the US president heard Carney state that he did “not seek power to dominate others”, and was “not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great power rival – only with better manners”. The dig was pointed, the style was effortless.

Carney’s team write great speeches, and the Harvard-educated economist with a doctorate from Oxford delivers them well. But one senses he’s much more than a good autocue reader. He dropped a couple of German rhetorical phrases into his Strasbourg speech and built a strong historical context, drawing on the ties that have bound Canada and Europe from the first world war onwards, creating a memorable picture of the seeds brought back to Canada from [Vimy Ridge](https://www.warmuseum.ca/articles/the-battle-of-vimy-ridge-april-9-to-12-1917) (where Canadian troops won a hard-fought battle in 1917 with heavy losses) and then replanted in France a century later.

While evocative historical links underpinned his sentiment, the vision for a brighter, shared future brought hope where Trump sows only disquiet. My academic colleague [Katie McGettigan](https://pure.royalholloway.ac.uk/en/persons/katie-mcgettigan/), speaking at a [British Library event](https://events.bl.uk/events/america-now-a-special-relationship), summed up Carney astutely, calling him “the new moral centre”. And, to date, he has backed his rhetoric with action.

This is far from an easy time for Canada. A trade war with its nearest neighbour and by far its largest trading partner is the last thing it needs. Clearly Carney recognises that an unbound Trump, surrounded by sycophants in his administration, is simply too capricious to engage with through the norms of rational diplomacy.

**As Carney first stated in Davos, and emphasised last week, the best way to bolster against irrational imperialism is through collective power. The Canadian certainly polished his credentials as the emerging middle power leader.**

Trump is no orator – and currently a long way from the moral centre. As at [Vimy Ridge](https://vimyfoundation.ca/learn/vimy-ridge), Carney innately understands the value in holding the high ground.

items.title: Wild Boston Globe Article Going Viral In Context Section Below
items.text:
The August 31 Instagram post from Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue, a lesbian bar in Greenfield, was upbeat, teasing a new DJ lineup and a volunteer meetup. But partway down the rainbow-hued [post](https://www.instagram.com/p/DcuMdvRq7uI/?hl=en "https://www.instagram.com/p/DcuMdvRq7uI/?hl=en") labeled “UPDATES!” was a sentence that would splinter the queer community in this small Pioneer Valley city and beyond.

“It is with love we inform our immunocompromised disabled divas we will be opening Saturday nights as mask *optional,*” wrote Last Ditch.

Previously, patrons were required to wear a well-fitted KN-95 mask “or better” at all times.

The new policy was not received with love.

“Just say you’re being complicit in a mass disabling event and get it over with,” wrote one commenter.

“people like you kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience,” posted another.

“I hope your venue gets firebombed for robbing my fellow immunocompromised people of their Saturday plans just to scrape extra revenue from ablists \[sic],” wrote a third.

The thread grew to 442 comments, some supportive, but many furious. The people running the bar were accused of being ableist — eugenicist, even — for relaxing their signature policy in the face of what commenters consider an ongoing pandemic (Greenfield [hasn’t reported any COVID cases](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/covid-19-reporting#covid-19-weekly-public-health-report- "https://www.mass.gov/info-details/covid-19-reporting#covid-19-weekly-public-health-report-") in more than two months).

Two days later, Last Ditch posted [an apology](https://www.instagram.com/p/DczislEFC56/?hl=en&img_index=1 "https://www.instagram.com/p/DczislEFC56/?hl=en&img_index=1"). “We are sorry for our passive and dismissive tone of our change to the norms and schedule impacting the most intersectional of us,” management wrote on Instagram. “We understand everyone faces different intersections and we are always working to consider all needs fully.”

Instead of defusing the situation, the apology seemed to make things worse. The bar had erred: it posted an Instagram card without providing alt-text for the visually impaired. This set off a fresh round of accusations of ableism.

“This is not an accessible post,” wrote one user. “It indicates the lack of care or interest in Disability intersectionality.”

Quaint, crunchy Greenfield (population 17,700) isn’t a bad place for a COVID-cautious lesbian bar in 2026, all things considered. Rainbow flags deck store windows downtown. On a recent weekend, a community theater was advertising a workshop for masked performers, down the street from a bookstore with a “medical masks required” sign in the window. Men in ponytails and N-95s were ordering hibiscus tea from the coffee shop off the main square.

Greenfield is close, both physically and spiritually, to Northampton, sometimes referred to as “Lesbianville, U.S.A.” In the Pioneer Valley, “every bar is a lesbian bar,” a friend who lives there told me.

Nevertheless, [Last Ditch](https://lastditchvenue.com/ "https://lastditchvenue.com/"), which opened last year as a bar for “dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers, and their friends,” is struggling.

Three housemates in their mid-20s opened it together, hoping to fill the void left by two local queer bars that had shuttered. One of the trio, Asa Rosario, a drag performer who uses it/its pronouns, envisioned a venue where it and its friends could perform.

The three were intentional about the kind of values they wanted to bring to the divey basement bar, which they decorated with discoveries from Facebook Marketplace and pieces from local artists. No one would be turned away from the space for lack of funds. “Poor and unhoused people are welcome in the space.” [The police were not](https://recorder.com/2025/09/30/last-ditch-bar-entry-ban/ "https://recorder.com/2025/09/30/last-ditch-bar-entry-ban/").

“Our mission is to create systems of care and action and aid,” says Jackie Matellian, one of the founders.

When it first opened, Last Ditch did fairly well. Customers fondly remember a raucous opening night with a (clothed) simulation of a lesbian sex act — masks in place — on the dance floor.

But over time, foot traffic to the bar slowed. More and more visitors said they didn’t have the cover fee; the bar let them in anyway. The owners fell behind on bills and couldn’t pay themselves or the people who worked there. So, after consulting with the Massachusetts LGBT Chamber of Commerce, they came up with a plan to bend one of their rules — and hopefully attract more customers.

But by the time of Last Ditch’s monthly community meeting on September 11, only one of the original founders, Matellian, is still involved. The two others stepped back from the daily operation months before, Matellian says, citing various pressures and health issues. One had enrolled in clown school.

There are some 10 people, seated in a circle on the dance floor, all wearing masks: Matellian, a handful of volunteers, some bar patrons, and two designated mediators who will facilitate conversations between parties who disagree. Another 10 or 15 people join the meeting via Zoom. The plan is to go clockwise, sharing views on the masking decision and the financial future of the bar. Each person has two minutes to speak. It begins with a calming breath exercise.

Almost immediately, the proceedings are derailed.

One of Last Ditch’s most vocal critics, the head of another queer COVID-conscious collective in Western Massachusetts, a performer and artist who goes by Soe Noire, has been posting complaints about Last Ditch for days. Now, Noire joins the meeting on Zoom. He and other critics begin to flood the Zoom chat with irate messages, which are dutifully read aloud to the group.

When it comes time for one of the mediators, a licensed therapist, to speak, she takes a conciliatory tone.

“I love that you are here online,” she says. But “these platforms alienate us from each other. I’m talking about social media.” She asks whether participants can try to remove themselves from “places of righteousness.”

“I would love to get to a place where we all know each other’s face, where we all know each other’s name,” she continues.

“It’s messed up that the mediator is dismissing those attending virtually. That’s not accessibility,” someone responds in the chat.

“A lot of people are calling for an acknowledgment of harm and I’m hearing a WHITE therapist ... center\[ing] the feelings of a majority white and white adjacent staff,” writes Noire, who is Black.

Moreover, the Zoom attendees speculate that the mediator’s licensed status makes her a mandated reporter — an agent of the state, akin to police. One person going by “Moss” asks if the mediator could have them hospitalized against their will, adding that her presence is “wildly unsafe.”

![Two people at a bar wearing KN-95 face masks. The person on the right is sitting on a bar stool and the person on the left is standing facing the person who is sitting and gesturing with their right hand.](https://bostonglobe-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/resizer/v2/CTJDPPL62RDIFB2B3BTXZZCKGA.jpg?auth=9febd2b6646f066a59cb186440a73e40df8a2ccd9ce775a8a4f856576aceec58&width=1440)

When Matellian’s turn comes to speak, she begins haltingly. She had never envisioned running Last Ditch alone. “It was not my passion project,” she says. “My main goal was to support Sage and Asa,” the other two founders. Her voice cracks.

“I never really wanted to do this,” Matellian says, beginning to cry under her mask. “I don’t think I’m doing a very good job.”

Matellian tells the group her credit score is trashed. For six months, she lived in her truck because she was pouring money into the bar. She is working four different jobs. She is responsible for paying off the $50,000 loan the three took out to launch the business.

The online critics are unmoved. “\[Y]ou chose to use your time to spill tears and center your feelings,” Noire posts in the chat. “This is incredibly racist and deflecting behavior.”

Eventually, after 3½ hours of discussion, the meeting wraps up. Noire has more to say, but when someone suggests he come to the next community meeting, he refuses. “There’s a lot of emotional and physical labor that goes into this, so for you as a white person that asks for me to stay for another meeting for free,” he says, is “incredibly disingenuous and racist. I’m not doing that.”

“Then I think, unfortunately, this meeting has failed you,” replies a facilitator, “and I’m sorry.”

The in-person participants file up the metal stairs, past the native plant garden, and out to their cars. Little has been resolved. Last Ditch’s landlord wants $3,900 in back rent by Monday.

Noire spends the hours after the meeting posting furious Instagram stories about Matellian and Last Ditch. Matellian (who uses she/they pronouns) had been shedding “WHITE THEY THEM TEARS,” he writes. The bar was not “a safe environment nor interested in revolutionary praxis.”

![A corner in the Last Ditch Bar with a lamp and a mirror. On the wall, there's some art, a bulletin board with various papers and cards on it, and a dart board. Under the dartboard there's a low shelf with books on it.](https://bostonglobe-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/resizer/v2/LYUQTUKDHFGQRCZ52UOZGARPOU.jpg?auth=f1e62dc8bc45585f0f9295e43a930288a9668f442ecca44bf1ce0b4695da12d7&width=1440)

I reach Noire, who identifies as a gender-expansive lesbian and uses he/him pronouns, by Zoom a few days later. I ask whether he has any sympathy for those running Last Ditch, given the profound financial strain they are under. “No,” he replies. (Noire asked to be referred to by his stage name because he says he has been stalked and fears for his safety.) “I’m not going to give grace” when someone is “spreading rhetoric that can and will get people hurt,” he says, referring to the fact that the bar’s account had “liked” a few comments supporting the relaxed rule.

Moreover, the mask policy change promotes “these ableist ideas that disabled people, immunocompromised people, should either risk their health or just be pushed out of spaces,” he says.

Noire, who lives about 50 minutes south of Greenfield, estimates he has visited the bar seven or eight times. But he won’t return unless there is new leadership. “You can’t repair a house that’s on fire,” he says.

Saturday, September 12, is the second weekly mask-optional night at Last Ditch.

Down a set of stairs, in a small concrete courtyard, a few people mill outside smoking. Another handful linger inside near the bar, under string lights. The dance floor, a wide checkered expanse with a stripper pole at the center, is empty.

Matellian is one of the few people wearing a mask; I talk with her and another volunteer, Melody Young, in a small library tucked inside an alcove by the bar, filled with zines and lesbian classics such as *Stone Butch Blues.* This is also their “free store,” which carries food, clothes, fentanyl test strips, Narcan, literature about STIs, and other supplies. Above us hangs a sign: “PROM CANCELLED ’CUZ LESBIANS.”

I remember a comment on Last Ditch’s original announcement, after the pile-on had begun: @scream_guy_wazzzuuuuuuup asked, “i’m sorry, all 400 of these crazy people live in GREENFIELD MASSACHUSETTS????”

I ask whether the people behind the angriest posts have genuine connections to the bar — are they real customers?

Young and Matellian say yes, they know many of the detractors.

“There are people that are close to us and love us who are really disappointed in our decision, and that is completely understandable,” says Young, who says her sister is one of the vocal critics online. “Like, it’s so understandable why they feel hurt by the way we did it and the fact that we did it.”

“They have passion for the space,” Matellian adds.

A number of people on Instagram also said they were excited to visit the space unmasked. But this night, the hoped-for other patrons haven’t materialized, despite $10 cocktails and sternum-shivering dance tracks from DJ Harsh Noise Boyfriend.

At the queer bar that occupied this space before Last Ditch (where masks were not required), a night like this might have drawn a hundred people, estimates Mixxy, the bartender on duty that night. A trans woman with thick black eyeliner and catlike poise, Mixxy is closeted in her day job as an engineer. She loves the bar enough to work for just tips, knowing Last Ditch is in the red. But she thinks the early dogmatism about masks was a mistake. People don’t like to feel scolded, she says. “That’s not how hospitality works.”

![A little corner in the bar where there's a small shelf with some items on it and a couple of baskets hanging on the wall with pamphlets and other materials. A sign in the middle of the wall says "free store."](https://bostonglobe-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/resizer/v2/WJXYA4BANNH3ZFDSRISWU65QCA.jpg?auth=7ce7fef2ce6775688990e5079c789aae3bdb01e3eb3674b08bade32e80bac1d0&width=1440)

Just after midnight, one patron is left at the bar, a regular who works at the Mexican restaurant next door. She wonders aloud about holding a Lady Gaga themed night, but Mixxy demurs. “Gaga is canceled,” she says. “Gaga is Zionist.”

The DJ is still playing EDM, and Matellian is alone on the checkered dance floor, making pensive, graceful loops on the stripper pole, KN-95 mask in place.

Matellian doesn’t expect the conflict at Last Ditch to end soon. She plans to co-operatize the bar, so she doesn’t bear so much financial liability, but that will come with its own challenges. And the discord about masking is unlikely to go away.

But it comes with the territory, she says. “There’s conflict, but we just hope that there’s more repair than conflict.”

“That’s the price you pay to be in community,” Matellian says.

items.title: SignerOS 1.3.0: Turn a regular PC into an offline Bitcoin signing device
items.text:
Hi again,

I have been working on SignerOS for some time and I just released **v1.3.0**.

SignerOS is an air-gapped Bitcoin signing system that runs from a USB stick. The idea is simple: use a regular PC as an offline Bitcoin signing device and wallet creation device.

It is a very minimal Buildroot-based Linux system. There is no network support and no desktop environment. The signing application is basically the whole system.

It runs from RAM and does not install anything to the PC. You boot it, use it, and shutdown the PC when you are finished. It never touch the hard-drive.

After my previous post, some people here took a look at the project and gave me some good feedback. One of the comments also pointed out some things about the change validation, especially for multisig and P2WSH/P2SH scripts.

So I did another review of this part of the code and made some improvements in v1.3.0.

Some of them:

* **Better script validation:** Before, SignerOS was mainly looking for your public key inside the script. Now it reads the script and checks what the script actually does.
* **Better multisig validation:** For 2-of-2, 2-of-3 and other multisig wallets, SignerOS checks the real public keys of the cosigners instead of trusting a wallet description or label in the PSBT.
* **All inputs are checked:** While working on this, I also found a case where one valid input could make a fake change output look valid. Now all inputs are checked to make sure they belong to the same wallet.
* **Timelocks:** Fixed some problems in how timelocked scripts are handled.
* **More warnings:** There are also some new warnings for multisig change outputs which are valid, but may not be recognized by some wallet software.

I think the most important part of this release is that SignerOS is now better at checking **"is this change really mine?"** before signing.

Thanks to everyone who is interested in the project, tested it, reviewed the code, reported issues and sent donations.

The feedback from the previous post was very useful for me. I originally made SignerOS for my own use, so it is really helpful to have other people looking at it too.

items.text:
![](https://m.stacker.news/158419)

I’ve put together a [catalogue](https://github.com/bitcoin-data/invalid-blocks) and a corresponding [post](https://deadmanoz.xyz/posts/2026/invalid-blocks) detailing 143 Bitcoin blocks that met the required proof-of-work target but failed a consensus rule, from the 2010 overflow to two previously unreported F2Pool timestamp failures from 2026!!

The catalogue brings together the surviving evidence for each case, so anyone can independently verify which consensus rule the block broke.

A few findings:

* **The two F2Pool headers from April and July this year have timestamps roughly 7 and 14 days below their parents’ median time past.** Both were found in merge-mined auxiliary chains; neither has a known Bitcoin-side capture.
* **Auxiliary chains preserve 49 of the 143 headers**, and provide the catalogue’s only recorded observation for 35. They check their own rules, so they can preserve evidence of candidates that Bitcoin peers reject.
* **89 blocks contain the same P2SH-invalid transaction**, mined between April and July 2012. Archived transaction lists and preserved headers establish its inclusion in each.
* **127 of the 143 have no complete body.** The surviving headers, coinbases or transaction inclusion proofs, together with chain context, still establish the failures.
* Another 10 reported cases remain separate because the evidence is insufficient.

The same merge mining research also recovered roughly 1,400 stale headers new to the [stale-blocks collection](https://github.com/bitcoin-data/stale-blocks). Merge mining has proved to be a productive side channel for both stales and invalids, and monitoring those chains is essential to a holistic Bitcoin monitoring effort.

In my [merge mining monitor](https://mmm.deadmanoz.xyz/) tool you can step through all invalid-blocks discovered in the merge-mined record (note that invalid blocks are currently called error blocks, this was the language I originally used):

![](https://m.stacker.news/158420)

If you have old node files, pool logs or other records that could fill a gap, contributions and corrections are very welcome.

[Vanilla cake with strawberries]([https://zap.cooking/r/naddr1qq08vctwd9kxccfdvdskkefdwa5hg6pdwd68ycthvfjhyunfv4esygyezxdl2trmyu2zwzmdxf2x0wl5hlcry0he39dn53xekmu39azwhupsgqqqw4rs29ydf0](https://zap.cooking/r/naddr1qq08vctwd9kxccfdvdskkefdwa5hg6pdwd68ycthvfjhyunfv4esygyezxdl2trmyu2zwzmdxf2x0wl5hlcry0he39dn53xekmu39azwhupsgqqqw4rs29ydf0))

Ingredients:
4 eggs
200 g unsalted butter
300 ml milk
500 g wheat flour
250 g of sugar
15 g of baking powder
a teaspoon of vanilla essence
a teaspoon of rum (optional)
Strawberries to taste

35x25 cm mold
6 people

In a bowl, add the 4 eggs, melted butter, milk, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Beat with a mixer at high speed until all the ingredients are combined.

Add the sifted flour and baking powder to the liquid mixture. Add the vanilla and rum essence. Beat until smooth and free of lumps.

Line the tray with parchment paper and add the mixture.

Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Chop the strawberry into pieces and add it to the mixture.

Bake for 30 minutes at 180°C.

items.title: My hot water mines Bitcoin and cooks food, with canola oil
items.text:
Cooking hash-vide style rabbit ramen with Bitcoin mining hot water heater
![](https://i.nostr.build/DxEDnACpHbOLPlsj.jpg)
![](https://i.nostr.build/564O7dCiXywaJLhI.jpg)
The second meal cooked in the Bitcoin mining hot water heater is rabbit ramen soup. Rabbit grown and harvested right here at the homestead, along with these other ingredients from the homestead rabbit stock, garlic, and finally golden oyster mushrooms dehydrated with a Bitcoin miner. Soy sauce, rice vinegar, lemon, sesame oil, Japanese seven spice, salt, pepper, butter.
![](https://i.nostr.build/bt4MMdkGF6VhrwFA.jpg)
![](https://i.nostr.build/a93EXzTlzoyqpgxj.jpg)
All ingredients went into a silicone bag and submerged in the hot canola oil tank of the bitcoin mining hot water heater for 3 days. Hard to beat mining Bitcoin, heating water, and cooking food all at the same time. I can get the water up to 150f out of the tap with only 1500w of power consumption for the total system, miner, pumps, and all!
![](https://i.nostr.build/6ePvU2b04Qm18jmw.jpg)
![](https://i.nostr.build/I08DfaYut91fThoi.jpg)
Another super cool aspect of this mining setup is that it runs on 110v power instead of 220v. Not having access to a 220v circuit is often a limiting factor for pleb miners, especially when these sorts of applications don't always require so much power. By modifying the apw12 PSU and making a custom power cord, now I can plug the miner into an existing 110v circuit. It cost less than $20 to do the modification on the PSU plus using a modified apw12 vs a Loki + apw3++ allows for voltage attenuation and higher total power output.
